page: Google Cloud Platform n4d-standard-48 is a general-purpose server instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9B45 processor. It features 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 24 physical cores with multithreading enabled, delivering 2.0 threads per core. The system is equipped with 192 GB of RAM, maintaining a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per core. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the CPU includes a cache configuration of 48 KB L1d, 1.0 MB L2, and 32 MB L3 cache. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it is provisioned with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong compute and memory performance. The AMD EPYC processor achieves top-tier single-core performance in stress-ng tests and gzip compression, placing in the top 10% of tested hardware. Multi-core performance is also strong, ranking in the top 25% for stress-ng multi-core, bzip3 decompression, and PassMark CPU scores. Memory bandwidth for small cached blocks is strong, though large block read and write operations fall into the average tier. The server demonstrates high efficiency in cryptographic and integer operations, supported by hardware-level instruction sets like AVX-512 and AES.

Given its balanced resource allocation and strong CPU capabilities, the n4d-standard-48 offers solid qualitative cost efficiency for general-purpose workloads that require high CPU throughput without massive memory footprints. It is highly capable for tasks such as web serving, database operations, and text processing, as evidenced by its strong PassMark database and Redis SET performance. Additionally, the instance performs exceptionally well in lightweight machine learning tasks, achieving top-tier inference speeds for small language models.
